messages.author: 669fc681030eaa53
messages.subject: Half-normal prior
parts:
Hello,

Is it possible to specify half-normal (or other half-distributions) in blavaan? It seems pretty straight-forward more generally in rstan, but I'm not seeing how it might work in blavaan. 

Thanks!
Garret

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Half-normal prior
parts: Is it possible to specify half-normal (or other half-distributions) in blavaan? It seems pretty straight-forward more generally in rstan, but I'm not seeing how it might work in blavaan.

Yes, if you export the Stan syntax (using target = "stanclassic").  But I don't think the newer (faster) Stan model---which is based on marginal covariance structure analysis rather than sampling factor scores as parameters---can handle any other types of prior than the ones shown in dpriors() output.  To see how to change parameters of the priors for individual parameter(s) or defaults for a type of parameter, see here:

https://faculty.missouri.edu/~merklee/blavaan/prior.html

You can find other helpful pages under the Examples menu at the top of that blavaan site.

I tried specifying a normal for SDs using the old Stan model, which should be truncated already when the parameter is defined, but it didn't work:

HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939,
            target = "stanclassic",
            dp = dpriors(theta = "normal(0, 1)[sd]"))


So I think you would just have to export the Stan syntax using the mcmcfile= argument to modify the model yourself.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Half-normal prior
parts:
I dont think you can do that with target="stan" for now.

Another approach, is that you could use the hypothesis() function from brms. To evaluate what proportion of the posterior distribution of a specific regression is positive/negative, called p-direction sometimes


library(blavaan)
library(brms)


model <- '
  # latent variable definitions
     ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
     dem60 =~ y1 + a*y2 + b*y3 + c*y4
     dem65 =~ y5 + a*y6 + b*y7 + c*y8

  # regressions
    dem60 ~ ind60
    dem65 ~ ind60 + dem60

  # residual correlations
    y1 ~~ y5
    y2 ~~ y4 + y6
    y3 ~~ y7
    y4 ~~ y8
    y6 ~~ y8
'

## unique priors for mv intercepts; parallel chains
fit <- bsem(model, data=PoliticalDemocracy, std.lv=T)
summary(fit)


mcs <- as.matrix(blavInspect(fit, "mcmc"))
dim(mcs)
head(mcs)

pt <- partable(fit)
subset(pt, op == "~")

hypothesis(mcs, "bet_sign[1] > 0")
hypothesis(mcs, "bet_sign[2] > 0")
hypothesis(mcs, "bet_sign[3] > 0")

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Half-normal prior
parts:
On Thu, 2020-10-29 at 08:37 -0400, Garret Hall wrote:
I’m interested in a half-normal prior for a regression coefficient I’m expecting to be positive, but I’m not certain just how strong it might be. It sounds like the truncated prior would work. Is there a way to do that with Stan priors without working directly with the Stan model as Terrence suggested?

I believe this will be problematic for a regression coefficient, because you also have to define lower and upper bounds for each parameter in Stan, and blavaan will always consider a regression coefficient to be unbounded.

You might consider a normal prior (or some other unbounded distribution, for jags or stanclassic) with nearly all its density above 0, which I think would better match the advice of the Stan developers (who recommend avoiding priors with hard boundaries). See "General principles" here:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Prior-Choice-Recommendations

Ed
